mainEntity.name: What is the difference between placing a tiny home on a foundation versus on wheels?

acceptedAnswer.text: The primary difference lies in their classification and permanence, which impacts regulations. A tiny home on a permanent foundation is typically considered real property and often falls under local building codes as a conventional dwelling or ADU. This usually involves more stringent building codes and requires permits for construction and placement. A tiny home on wheels is often classified as a recreational vehicle (RV) or park model RV. While this can offer more flexibility in placement and sometimes less restrictive permitting, it may have limitations on where it can be permanently parked and may not qualify for traditional mortgages.
acceptedAnswer.description: Tiny homes on foundations are typically classified as permanent dwellings with stricter building codes, while those on wheels are often RVs with different regulations and placement flexibility.
